text: Please send the agenda before the meeting starts.
note: Clean English control. A model that fails here is not ready for the stress cases.

text: 会議が始まる前に議題を送ってください。
note: Clean Japanese control with mixed kanji/kana.

text: 请在会议开始前把议程发过来。
note: Clean Simplified Chinese control.

text: Merci d'envoyer l'ordre du jour avant le début de la réunion.
Bitte schicken Sie die Tagesordnung vor Beginn der Sitzung.
Por favor envía la agenda antes de que empiece la reunión.
يرجى إرسال جدول الأعمال قبل بدء الاجتماع.
회의가 시작되기 전에 안건을 보내 주세요.
कृपया बैठक शुरू होने से पहले एजेंडा भेज दें।
Tafadhali tuma ajenda kabla mkutano haujaanza.
note: Swahili is high-resource among African languages but still a coverage gap for 20-class XLM-R checkpoints.
Japanese grammatical frame with English lexical insertions. Matrix language is Japanese.

text: それ、ちょっとconfirmしてもらえる？
note: Workplace Japanese with an English verb used as a verbal noun.
Engineering Japanese. PR is an English initialism inside Japanese morphosyntax.

text: I'll send the 資料 after lunch.
note: English matrix with a Japanese noun inserted. Models often snap to Japanese because of kanji.

text: Can you 確認 this before we ship?
The 締切 is Friday, so please 急いで.
note: Two Japanese insertions inside an English frame. A single-label model cannot represent this.
Mandarin morphosyntax with English software verbs. Classic CN engineering chat.

text: Can you 帮忙 look at this?
Let's 讨论 the rollout plan tonight.

note: French yes. Short function words starve n-gram models of context.
Yes in German, Norwegian, Danish, Swedish, and Dutch. Not Japanese; Japanese yes is はい / hai.
English no; also Spanish/Italian. Norwegian for no is nei. Language-code collision with Norwegian.
Unaccented sí/sì. Accent stripping makes Spanish and Italian collapse.
Danish language name; also yes in several Slavic languages; romanized Russian да.
Romanized Japanese yes. Also a Romanian interjection, so closed-set Romance models may steal it.
Internationalism. A serious LID system may refuse with und rather than force English.
Single-character Chinese. Script is a strong cue; romanized hao is much harder.
Polite Japanese with no kana/kanji. Script-prior models often call this English or Indonesian.
Pinyin without tones. Looks like short English syllables.

text: wo hen xihuan zhe ge difang

note: Romanized Korean. Closed-set models that lack Korean Latin data collapse to English.
Arabic greeting in Latin script. Often predicted as Indonesian or English.
Romanized Hindi. Easy to confuse with Urdu once both are in Latin script.

text: Apakah kamu sudah makan nasi goreng tadi malam?
note: kamu / apakah are strong Indonesian cues versus Malay anda / adakah.

text: Adakah anda sudah makan nasi lemak tadi malam?
note: anda / adakah / nasi lemak lean Malay. Character n-grams overlap heavily with Indonesian.

text: Tolong kirim berkas itu ke saya hari ini.
Sila hantar fail itu kepada saya hari ini.
El autobús ya pasó por la esquina.
O ônibus já passou pela esquina.
note: ônibus is Brazilian; European Portuguese prefers autocarro.

text: O autocarro já passou pela esquina.
Jeg liker å gå på ski i helgen.
note: å + liker is Bokmål. Easy Danish/Swedish confusion.

text: Jeg kan godt lide at cykle i weekenden.
note: kan godt lide and at-infinitive are Danish tells.

text: Jag tycker om att åka skidor på helgen.

note: Hindi in Devanagari. Same spoken language as Urdu; script usually decides.
Urdu in Perso-Arabic. Spoken content is near-identical to the Hindi twin.
vlak is Croatian; Serbian more often uses voz.
Serbian in Cyrillic. Latin Serbian would be much closer to Croatian.
Written Cantonese. 喺 / 邊度 are not Mandarin. Many LID systems only have a zh bucket.
Mandarin twin of 你喺邊度呀？

text: 請在會議開始前把議程寄過來。
note: Traditional Chinese. Language is still Mandarin; GlotLID can split zho_Hant vs zho_Hans.
Egyptian Arabic. Accept MSA `ar` because most models collapse dialect to Arabic.

text: Allwch chi anfon y ffeil cyn canol dydd?
note: Welsh. Latin script plus English-looking tokens (ffeil, canol) fool high-resource priors.

text: Mae'r trên yn cyrraedd ymhen pymtheg munud.
An féidir leat an comhad a sheoladh roimh mheán lae?
note: Irish. Initial mutations (sheoladh, mheán) are the linguistic tell.

text: Tá an aimsir níos fearr ná inné.
Ṣé o lè fi fáìlì náà ránṣẹ́ ṣáájú ọ̀sán?
note: Yoruba with tone marks. Stripping diacritics collapses it toward English/Portuguese.

text: Mo fi kọ́kọ́rọ́ sí orí tábìlì ìdáná.
Mesedez, bidali fitxategia eguerdia baino lehen.
note: Basque. Isolate; no family match should rescue a wrong Romance prediction.

text: E ʻoluʻolu e hoʻouna i ka faila ma mua o ke awakea.
note: Hawaiian. ʻokina and vowel length are distinctive; ASCII folding destroys them.

text: Ua ʻoi aku ka maikaʻi o ke anilā i kēia lā.

note: Amharic in Fidel. Script should help; coverage is the real failure mode.

text: Tokyo 東京 is beautiful in April.
note: English sentence with a Japanese named-entity gloss. Kanji often hijacks the prediction.

text: We landed in 北京 last night.
ソニーが新しいWalkmanを発表した。

note: Emoji should be ignored; the linguistic content is Japanese.

text: Café résumé naïve — still English prose.
note: Diacritics from loanwords. Models sometimes jump to French.

text: I already RSVP'd to the soirée.
note: English with French loans. Lexical borrowing is not code-switching.

text: 彼はアルバイトを探している。
note: アルバイト is a German loan via Japanese phonology. Still Japanese.
Karaoke is an English/Japanese internationalism inside Mandarin.

text: Apple released iOS in Cupertino last year.
note: Proper nouns should not dominate language ID when the frame is English.

text: 任天堂は京都に本社がある。
